subject: Proposed availability carveout + monthly remedy clarification
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir.desai@rivetcloud.com>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@rivetcloud.com
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: carveout for scheduled batch maintenance + monthly remedy question

Diego,

Thanks for the call yesterday — quick follow-up from our side. As we move toward a final SOW, the procurement and ops teams at RivetCloud want to confirm two things before we sign:

1) Maintenance carveout: our workload includes a daily 30–90 minute batched window (early morning PST) where latency is higher by design. We need that window to be explicitly excluded from the monthly uptime calculation for the first 12 months of the contract.

2) Monthly remedy: your standard SLA lists credits tied to % uptime bands. For our internal budgeting we need clarity on how credits are calculated when multiple short degradations occur across the month (e.g., three 20-minute degradations vs. one 60-minute outage). Specifically: is remedy prorated by incident, or aggregated as total downtime?

Attached is a redline of the SLA template with our proposed carveout language and a marked-up remedy table. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept language that allows a daily maintenance carveout and also how the remedy aggregation works?

Appreciate a concise note so procurement can proceed.

Best,
Samir Desai
Head of Platform Ops
RivetCloud

Attachments: rivet_sla_redline_2025-08-25.pdf
From: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Desai <samir.desai@rivetcloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Aug 2025 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for scheduled batch maintenance + monthly remedy question

Samir — thanks for sending this over and for the clear redlines. Quick answers up front, then internal notes below:

- Maintenance carveout: We can accommodate a daily scheduled maintenance carveout for the first 12 months, subject to: (a) window defined in the SOW (start/end times), (b) a maximum of 7 maintenance events per month, and (c) a commitment that the window is used only for the batched ETL/maintenance workload (not unplanned failovers).

- Remedy aggregation: Our standard practice is to calculate monthly remedy on total measured downtime across the month (i.e., aggregate minutes). That means multiple short degradations sum toward the monthly total. For visibility, we can provide an incident-level CSV export each month showing start/end timestamps for each measured degradation.

I'll loop in Legal for the exact carveout wording. Laura — can you confirm the maximum-event cap language and whether we want to permit a one-time extension in month two if Rivet needs to shift the window? Aditya — can your infra team confirm that monthly CSV export is feasible from our telemetry pipeline (token-level uptime detection) and estimate any additional cost of keeping per-incident logs beyond 30 days?

Samir — if this approach looks acceptable I can circulate a clean SLA with the carveout language, the 7-event cap, and the aggregation model for remedy.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-sla-draft-v2.docx
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Aug 2025 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for scheduled batch maintenance + monthly remedy question

Diego / team — quick legal read. I redlined two small items in the proposed carveout:

1) Event cap as proposed (7/month) is fine, but we should add a ‘good faith notice’ requirement: Rivet must notify Redwood if they plan to exceed 3 events in any rolling 30-day window so we can coordinate capacity and avoid surprise tail-latency impacts.

2) One-time extension: I can accept a single, documented extension in month two, but it must be accompanied by a mutually agreed mitigation plan (e.g., increased pre-warming or dedicated burst pool for the shifted window).

For remedy aggregation: our preference is to keep aggregation across the month (simpler to operate and test). However, to address their budgeting ask, propose we add an illustrative example clause to the SLA showing how multiple short incidents roll up to a monthly credit (table + formula). That should reduce back-and-forth with procurement.

Monica — any compliance implications on retaining per-incident logs for 90 days vs. standard 30?

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, diego_fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Aug 2025 14:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: carveout for scheduled batch maintenance + monthly remedy question

Laura / team — retention note. From a compliance standpoint we can retain per-incident telemetry for 90 days with a small storage delta; operationally it helps for dispute resolution. There are no additional regulatory controls triggered by 90-day retention for Rivet’s profile. Cost impact: roughly +2% on telemetry storage on average for that customer class.

Next steps I recommend we:
- Push a clean SLA incorporating: carveout window language, 7-event cap, notice at 3 events/30d, one-time extension clause, and an illustrative remedy aggregation table.
- Offer the 90-day incident CSV export as an optional paid add-on (line item on SOW) but include a 30-day default export at no charge.
- Diego: propose you send the revised clean SLA and a short note showing the two example aggregation scenarios requested by procurement (three 20-min degradations vs. one 60-min outage) so they can budget.

I can approve the legal language once the clean SLA hits my inbox.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Director, Commercial Ops (Legal Liaison)
Redwood Inference
